# Where citizen data can go

<!-- Generated by scripts/build-residency-doc.mjs from the declarations in
     src/server/core/residency.ts. Do not edit by hand: tests/residency.test.ts
     fails if this file and the code disagree. -->

Every destination a citizen's words, voice, photographs or telephone number
can reach, and what each one receives. This is the inventory a legal review
asks for, and it is generated from the same declarations the platform enforces
at runtime — so it cannot describe a system other than the one that is running.

## The position

The programme's intent is that everything stays in the Democratic Republic of
the Congo. There is no cloud region in the country, so the pilot runs from the
nearest available one and migrates when an in-country option exists. That is a
decision with a date on it, not a permanent posture, and this document exists so
that the gap between the intent and the deployment is stated rather than assumed.

## How it is enforced

`DATA_RESIDENCY` names the jurisdictions a deployment permits, as a comma-separated
list of ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes. A destination outside that set is **never
registered**: it has no code path, so no ordering, retry or fallback can reach it.
A message channel outside it returns a delivery failure, which the escalation path
reports and the readiness probe degrades on — the argument for changing the policy
or the carrier, made at the moment it matters rather than after an incident.

Unset means unrestricted. That is right on a laptop and is reported as a finding
in any deployment that serves citizens.

## What moving the container does not fix

A voice recording sent to a transcription service abroad has left the country
whether the server is in Johannesburg or in Kinshasa. The providers below are the
residency question; the hosting is the smaller half of it.

## The inventory

| Destination | Kind | Operator | Jurisdiction | On the safety path | What it receives |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `self` | The deployment itself | The programme, on the host it deploys to | same as the deployment (`DEPLOYMENT_JURISDICTION`) | yes | Everything: transcripts, translations, case notes, recordings, photographs, phone numbers (encrypted), safeguarding records. |
| `mock` | AI provider | The programme | same as the deployment (`DEPLOYMENT_JURISDICTION`) | yes | Nothing. The offline rules provider runs in the same process and makes no network call. |
| `anthropic` | AI provider | Anthropic PBC | US | no | The French pivot of what the citizen said, and the protocol context, for understanding and explanation. |
| `gemini` | AI provider | Google LLC | US | no | The citizen's words for understanding, and voice recordings for transcription. |
| `openai` | AI provider | OpenAI, L.L.C. — or a self-hosted endpoint when OPENAI_BASE_URL is set | US, or the declared location of a self-hosted endpoint (`AI_SELF_HOSTED_JURISDICTION`) | no | Voice recordings for transcription, the citizen's words for understanding, and text for speech synthesis. |
| `google_tts` | AI provider | Google LLC | US | no | The French or localised answer text, to be spoken. |
| `twilio` | Communication channel | Twilio Inc. | US | yes | The citizen's telephone number, call audio, SMS text, and WhatsApp messages where Twilio carries them. |
| `meta` | Communication channel | Meta Platforms, Inc. | US | yes | The citizen's telephone number, their messages, voice notes and photographs. |
| `africastalking` | Communication channel | Africa's Talking — declared base of operations, to be confirmed in procurement | KE (override with `AFRICASTALKING_JURISDICTION`) | yes | The citizen's telephone number and the text of reminders, answers and escalation notices. |
| `log` | Communication channel | The programme | same as the deployment (`DEPLOYMENT_JURISDICTION`) | no | Nothing. A message is written to this deployment's own log instead of being delivered. |

## What is lost if a destination is refused

- **`self`** — Nothing runs. This is the deployment itself.
- **`mock`** — The platform has no fallback and cannot answer at all.
- **`anthropic`** — Understanding of free speech degrades to the offline rules provider. Danger-sign detection and severity are unaffected — they never used a model.
- **`gemini`** — One fewer understanding and transcription provider in the chain.
- **`openai`** — No transcription: a voice call falls back to the fixed scripts and the keypad menu, and free speech is not understood.
- **`google_tts`** — Answers are spoken by the next configured synthesiser, or read from a recording where one exists.
- **`twilio`** — No voice, and no SMS or WhatsApp through this carrier. An escalation cannot reach a worker by telephone.
- **`meta`** — No WhatsApp channel.
- **`africastalking`** — No SMS. Reminders and escalation notices cannot be delivered by message.
- **`log`** — Nothing; a deployment that serves citizens already reports log-only delivery as a failure.

## The strictest useful setting

```
DATA_RESIDENCY=CD
DEPLOYMENT_JURISDICTION=CD
```

Every remote provider is refused. The platform still triages by protocol, still
detects danger signs, still grades severity and still speaks the fixed emergency
scripts — none of that ever used a model. What it loses is understanding free
speech and transcribing a voice note. That is a different product, and under a
strict localisation requirement it is the honest one.
